items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: When we got to Dallas we split up and went different ways and after I joined Troy's band, that's when we were playing in Wichita Falls

ctx.x: Well what about Herschel Evans then? Was he a good reader when he came?

No, Herschel couldn't read music. How I met Herschel Evans, I was getting ready to leave here and they used to have the Dixie Series and there was a band that Herschel came here with, with a team from Wichita Falls that year. The name of this band was the TNT band and Jimmy Westbrook was the drummer, he's a left-handed drummer. He's now living in Los Angeles and Herschel was playing alto and playing a date up at the old Pelican ball and I met Herschel then and we all left on the same train. I was going to Dallas…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: And that's when I was with Troy's band.

ctx.x: I know there are a lot of musical families around there.

Well, Oscar Pettiford, that's the band I was supposed to go with when I went to Troy's band. Oh, you were going with the Pettiford? They wanted me. And I had Richard McCarthy from here and Lucian Johnson. And I told them what I was going to do, so I told Richard, I said, Richard, I can get you in this little band if you want to stay. He wanted to come back to New Orleans. So I talked to Pettiford and he only just wanted me in the band. And I told him, no, I had already told Troy that I was going to join him and I…
Did you know the biases? Sure, all of them were there?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: when I was with Troy First, joined Troy Floyd's band, I didn't have too much time for solo work.

ctx.x: Well, some people are great readers but can't play, you know. That's true.

Yeah. A lot of, well, for instance, for a long time, when I was with Troy First, joined Troy Floyd's band, I didn't have too much time for solo work. Yeah. Most of mine was reading because the fellas in the band were limited. And of course, naturally, I had to play three, four, five different parts. Yeah. But as the band got older and we got to playing together, well then I could occasionally get out and solo.
Mm-hmm. Well, you must have been an awful good soloist, changing from the rapids. There's so many things.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: I took his place in Troy Floyd's band.

ctx.x: Well what about his style then? Beautiful. Great style. Did he sound the same as he did on the record with, say, LATER in 32?

I think he sounded better. I think he sounded better in person. One man that they weren't able to capture, I don't think, I've never heard anything from him, was Claude Benno Kennedy. I took his place in Troy Floyd's band. But he was not a powerful trumpet player.
